original_query: SELECT t0.JOB, t1.NAME FROM (SELECT EMPNO, ENAME, JOB, MGR, HIREDATE, SAL, COMM, DEPTNO, SLACKER, DEPTNO + EMPNO AS f9 FROM EMP WHERE ENAME = 'A') AS t0 LEFT JOIN (SELECT DEPTNO, NAME, DEPTNO + 5 AS f2 FROM DEPT) AS t1 ON t0.JOB = t1.NAME AND t0.f9 = t1.f2 GROUP BY t0.JOB, t1.NAME
rewritten_query:
SELECT DISTINCT
       e.JOB,
       d.NAME
FROM EMP e
LEFT JOIN DEPT d
  ON d.NAME = e.JOB
 AND d.DEPTNO = e.DEPTNO + e.EMPNO - 5
WHERE e.ENAME = 'A';

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Flatten the derived tables t0 and t1 by removing unused columns (MGR, HIREDATE, SAL, COMM, SLACKER from t0). The only needed columns are EMPNO, ENAME, JOB, DEPTNO from EMP and DEPTNO, NAME from DEPT.
Replace GROUP BY t0.JOB, t1.NAME with SELECT DISTINCT, since there are no aggregate functions and grouping by the same two output columns is semantically identical to DISTINCT.

Rewrite the computed join condition t0.f9 = t1.f2 into a sargable form: d.DEPTNO = e.DEPTNO + e.EMPNO - 5. This allows an index on DEPT(NAME, DEPTNO) to be used for a nested-loop join once the filtered EMP rows are small (~41 rows estimated vs 45M scanned).

Push the filter ENAME = 'A' directly into the main query WHERE clause and recommend a covering index CREATE INDEX ON emp (ename) INCLUDE (job, empno, deptno) to avoid a 45M-row parallel seq scan, which is the dominant cost.
